citation: Guino-o, R. S. II. (2012). Length-Weight and Length-Length Relationships and Fulton Condition Factor of Philippine Mullets (Family Mugilidae: Teleostei). Silliman Journal, 53(2), July–December 2012, 176–189.

accessReview.publisherRecord: The official Silliman Journal article record identifies Volume 53, Issue 2 (2012); the complete 14-page publisher PDF was accessed. The article page's later 2022 platform date is not the issue publication date.
accessReview.reuse: No article-specific open license was identified. Silliman Journal's editorial policy states that published-article copyright is held by the journal and individual authors and specifies permission conditions for reproducing article text, tables and figures. No structured-data or public-app reuse permission was established; table data were not transcribed.

evidenceScope.fieldworkDate: Pagatban River sampling is reported monthly from January through December 2011.
evidenceScope.waterbody: Pagatban River, Negros Oriental; the paper also describes the downstream estuary. This is a study locality, not coverage of every Negros or Visayas river.
evidenceScope.studyPurpose: Length-weight, length-length and condition-factor research on ten Philippine mullet taxa sampled across fourteen sites; it is not a whole-fish-community checklist.
evidenceScope.PagatbanSampling: The paper reports monthly fish collection in Pagatban using a seine net (printed mesh-size unit: 1 cm²), morphological identification and laboratory examination. The wider national-site collection approach differs from the Pagatban sampling method.
evidenceScope.reportedPagatbanDistribution: The discussion names three mullet taxa as documented in Pagatban; it describes one as extending into upper-midstream reaches and two as occurring only in the downstream estuary. This prose does not supply a complete river species inventory or a full station-by-month species matrix.
evidenceScope.coordinateHandling: A single collection-site coordinate is printed in the paper, but no datum or CRS is stated. It was not converted into or used as map geometry.
evidenceScope.dietEvidence: The reviewed paper is a morphometric and condition-factor study, not a stomach-content or diet study; it supports no natural-diet claims for Bangwit's diet feature.
evidenceScope.voucherAndTaxonomy: The author describes morphological identification using diagnostic traits and taxonomic guides and preservation of specimens in formalin/ethanol. No public voucher catalog number or specimen-level crosswalk was identified in the reviewed article.

relatedUnpublishedLead.citationStatus: A 2019 Bayawan River paper cites a 2010 Bucol and Carumbana Pagatban fish-recovery study as unpublished. Silliman University community news reports that the authors found 61 species in a 2010 survey, but the original report, species table, methods, site matrix and reuse terms were not found.
relatedUnpublishedLead.countUse: Discovery lead only; do not use as a verified checklist, current occurrence, regional coverage denominator or species count until the primary report and its methods are obtained and reviewed.

decision.use: Historical primary lead for a year-long, mullet-focused Pagatban sample and source for locating the underlying thesis/specimens. The 2010 recovery survey remains an unpublished-data lead reported second-hand.
decision.reason: The 2012 paper is taxonomically and ecologically narrower than a river checklist, includes downstream estuarine evidence, has no located article-specific open data license, and its printed coordinate lacks a stated datum. The 2010 61-species report is not available as a primary artifact.

limitations: The 2012 study covers mullets, not all fish families or a complete Pagatban River inventory.
The article's national sample summary combines fourteen localities and must not be mistaken for Pagatban-only data.
Freshwater reaches and the downstream estuary are described separately; estuarine taxa are not evidence of year-round freshwater residency.
A 2011 sample does not establish current occupancy, present abundance, legal catchability, fishing conditions or water safety.
No diet, prey, stomach-content, gear recommendation or bait claim is supported by this morphometric paper.
The original 2010 recovery report behind the secondary 61-species figure has not been obtained; its reported richness is not independently verified here.
No species table, figure, PDF, image, geometry, public occurrence, or app species row was copied or approved.
nextActions: Ask Silliman University/NORSU or the authors whether the 2010 Pagatban recovery report and its species-by-site data can be shared, and obtain methods, dates, stations, vouchers and reuse terms before adding any of its reported 61 taxa.

Request written guidance from Silliman Journal and the author before reproducing table-derived structured data in a public app; keep source attribution and license terms attached to any permitted derivative.
Use the 2012 paper only for its dated, study-specific claims after current taxonomy and station context are reviewed; do not treat it as complete Pagatban or regional coverage.
Continue the independent Negros source sweep for Ilog estuary/diverted-channel and Siaton freshwater studies; keep freshwater, brackish, estuary and coastal evidence partitioned.

references.supports: Official article record and issue metadata for Guino-o's Pagatban-linked mullet study.
Complete publisher PDF; article scope, 2011 Pagatban sampling, methods and river/estuary distribution statements.
